---
title: "How do I select a reproducible random sample of records?"
---

## Question

How do I select a reproducible random sample of records?

## Work through it

Identify the full set of eligible rows; set a sample size no larger than the available rows; sample without replacement and report the selection method.

## Worked example: iris

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("iris")
chosen <- ru_apply("sample_random", data=d, n=12, seed=42)
stopifnot(nrow(chosen)==12, identical(names(chosen),names(d)))
```

The selected rows are a reproducible simple random subsample of the 150 Iris records. This random selection does not make the original collection representative of all flowers.

## Adapt to another question

```r
ru_apply("sample_random", data=your_data, n=12, seed=42)
```

With-replacement sampling uses a different rule and can select a record more than once; do not confuse it with sampling without replacement.

Check the input conditions with `ru_plan("sample_random")` before treating a calculation as an inference.
